ITodoListUser.description:
Represents a single user account registered in the Todo List application.

Encapsulates all user-specific information such as unique email, authentication credentials (never reveals raw password or hash), lock status for moderation, and timestamps for account lifecycle (creation, update, soft deletion).

Used in user detail retrieval and update endpoints. Password hash is NEVER included in API exposures. Soft deletion is indicated via the deleted_at timestamp. Designed for end-user profile, account management, and administrative oversight with strict audit and security controls.

id.description: Primary Key. Universally unique identifier for the user.

email.description: Unique email address of the user. Used for login and system notifications. Must be unique across all users.

locked.description: Account lock status. True if the user is suspended or blocked by admin for policy or security reasons.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the user account was created.

updated_at.description: Timestamp for the most recent update to the user profile or credentials.

oneOf.description: Timestamp when the user was soft-deleted. Null if active.
Indicates the user has never been deleted.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp when the user was soft-deleted. Null if active.

email.description:
User email address to be registered.

Must be unique across all accounts. Used as login credential and notification address. Validated for standard email format and uniqueness before creating account. Business logic will reject duplicates or malformed addresses.

password.description:
Password for authenticating user account (plain text input; will be hashed).

Must meet complexity requirements—minimum 8 characters, mixture of letters and numbers. Actual hash will never be sent to or stored from client; this value is stored as a hash in the database. Used only during registration or login, never returned in responses.

ITodoListUser.ICreate.description:
Request payload for registering a new end user with the Todo List service.

Accepts user-provided email and password only. The password must meet length and complexity requirements; the email must be unique and valid by RFC standards. Account creation will fail if these constraints are not met. Additional onboarding is handled server-side.

ITodoListUser.IAuthorized.description:
Authentication result and authorization context for normal end users.

Returned upon successful login or token refresh. Contains all fields necessary for user session establishment, including the user ID and the JWT token pair.

Never includes any sensitive authentication credentials or password hashes.

id.description: Unique identifier of the authenticated todo_list_users account.

email.description: Unique email address of the user. Used for login and system notifications. Must be unique across all users.

locked.description: Account lock status. True if the user is suspended or blocked by admin for policy or security reasons.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the user account was created.

updated_at.description: Timestamp for the most recent update to the user profile or credentials.

oneOf.description: Timestamp when the user was soft-deleted. Null if active.
Indicates the user has never been deleted.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp when the user was soft-deleted. Null if active.

ITodoListUser.ILogin.description:
Login request for normal end users of the Todo List service.

Used by unauthenticated clients to provide user credentials (email and password) for authentication against the todo_list_users table. Only active, unlocked user accounts may successfully login via this type.

Implements business logic requirements for anti-bruteforce, account locked status, and password validation policy. Account lock and failure reasons are never exposed through this schema. Designed for public login endpoint that never returns sensitive system information.

Session context fields are included to support security auditing and device/session tracking, in line with system audit requirements.

email.description:
User email address for login. Must match an existing user's unique email as stored in the database.

Validated against RFC standards. Used as the primary identifier for authentication.

password.description:
Plaintext password provided by the user for authentication. Backend hashes and verifies this against the password_hash stored in the todo_list_users table.

Never stored or returned anywhere. Must comply with business password policy as enforced by the service layer.

oneOf.description: Client IP address for session and audit purposes. Optional - may be omitted or null if unknown.
Client IP address for session and audit purposes. Optional - may be omitted or null if unknown.

ip.description: Client IP address (v4 or v6) for session and audit records. Optional. If omitted or null, backend infers IP from request metadata. Used for security and regulatory logging.

href.description:
The page or resource URL where the login form was submitted. This is required for audit, session tracking, and is typically the full browser location.

Must be provided by the client. Enables traceability for login-originated sessions.

referrer.description:
The previous URL (HTTP Referrer) of the client before reaching the login page.

Required for session trail establishment and audit. If there is no referrer, clients must supply an empty string.

ITodoListUser.IRefresh.description:
Request body for the user JWT refresh operation.

Contains only the refresh token used to request new access/refresh JWT pairs for a previously authenticated end user session. Submitted by clients when existing access tokens expire or soon-to-expire and a valid refresh token is still present.

Security constraints and refresh policy enforcement must be handled by the backend as specified in requirements.

No other fields or credentials are accepted for this operation.

refresh_token.description:
The refresh token previously issued by the authentication service to this user session.

Must be valid and untampered at the time of use. Permits strict validation against expiry, revocation, and signature rules.

email.description: Unique email address of the admin for login. Email must be unique in the todo_list_admins table and is used for both login and notification. Must follow valid email format.

password.description: The admin's password in plain text. Must be at least 8 characters long and will be securely hashed before storage (never stored in plain text). Password strength policy applies.

ITodoListAdmin.IJoin.description:
Admin registration (join) request for the Todo List system.

Admin provides their unique email address and plain text password. Password must be at least 8 characters and is subjected to validation then hashed and stored in password_hash (never stored in plain text). Email address must be unique per database constraints. Account will be created as unlocked (locked: false) and timestamps will be set per system rules.

id.description: UUID identifier for admin as assigned in the todo_list_admins table.

email.description:
Unique email address of the admin for login and notification.

Must be unique across all administrator accounts. Used for authentication and official notifications related to privileged actions. Must not overlap normal users.

locked.description:
Admin account lock status.

Indicates if the administrator is currently suspended from system access. True if the account is locked for any reason (disciplinary, compliance, etc.), false if active.

role.description:
Administrative role or privilege class (e.g., superadmin, moderator).

Specifies the admin's permission tier and authorizes their scope of actions within the system. Determines access boundaries within admin workflows. Must match recognized roles per business policy.

created_at.description:
Account creation timestamp.

Datetime when the admin account was established in the system. Used for lifecycle tracking and audit history.

updated_at.description:
Time of last admin profile or credential update.

Tracks when any profile data or password was last changed. Supports record history and security audits.

oneOf.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the admin account.

If the admin account has been soft deleted, this field contains the datetime of deletion. Otherwise, it is null. Used for internal record management and compliance.

deleted_at.description: Soft deletion timestamp for the admin account or null if active.

ITodoListAdmin.IAuthorized.description: JWT-authenticated admin session information. Contains the admin's UUID and a newly issued JWT token pair for authentication and session management.

email.description: Unique email address associated with the admin account. Used for login and notification purposes. Must correspond to an active admin in the todo_list_admins table. Email addresses are unique within the system and not shared with regular users.

password.description: Plain-text password used for administrator authentication. Never stored in raw form; compared to the database-stored strong hash. Must meet system security policy for complexity and length—minimum eight characters, typically allowing up to 128. Only valid for currently active, non-locked, non-deleted admin accounts. Provided by the user at login.

ITodoListAdmin.ILogin.description:
DTO for admin login request credentials.

Contains the email address and plain-text password provided by an admin attempting to log in. The password is checked against the todo_list_admins schema record for the user with a matching email after secure hash validation. Used only for authentication and not stored or echoed. Inactive, locked, or deleted accounts (deleted_at not null) are denied access. Adheres to security best practices for credential validation and traceability.

refresh_token.description: Refresh token for renewing the JWT session of the authenticated admin account. Must be a currently valid token issued by the system. Tied to todo_list_admins session and subject to lock/deletion checks at validation time. Provided by the client when requesting token renewal.

ITodoListAdmin.IRefresh.description:
DTO for admin JWT refresh operation.

Contains the refresh token issued on successful initial login. Used only to acquire a new token pair, and never consumed for password-based authentication. Validation checks include ensuring the admin is not locked or deleted in todo_list_admins and that the token has not expired or been revoked.

ITodoListSystemConfig.description:
Represents a single global system configuration record for the Todo List application.

This type models the database entity from the todo_list_system_configs table, which stores global operational and feature configuration values. Each record is uniquely identified by its key and contains a value (as a string), an optional description, and audit fields for creation, update, and soft deletion. System configuration records are not user- or admin-specific—they apply globally to all users and system behaviors.

The audit properties—created_at, updated_at, deleted_at—capture the operational history and integrity of system-level behavior. Soft deletion enables rollback and full compliance with audit or restoration requirements.

id.description: Primary Key for the system configuration record. Each configuration is globally unique and referenced by this identifier within the database. Required for retrieval and mutation operations.

key.description: Unique configuration key identifying the system setting. Examples include 'default_timezone', 'feature_maintenance_mode', or other core options. Must be globally unique; enforced by a unique constraint. Used by API as both path parameter and business identifier.

value.description: The value for this configuration as a string. Generally represents an operational flag, system default, or feature toggle. May be a serialized representation for more complex options but is typically a scalar. Required for any configuration to be active.

description.description: Optional, human-readable documentation describing this configuration entry. May provide details about intent, operational purpose, or business context. This field supports maintenance and audit as free-form text.

created_at.description: Timestamp of creation for this config entry, recorded automatically for audit and operational monitoring. Format ISO 8601 date-time string (e.g., '2025-11-17T15:36:03.484Z').

updated_at.description: Timestamp of last update to this config entry. Tracked for system compliance and operational safety. Automatically managed by system.

deleted_at.description: If present, indicates the timestamp when this entry was soft-deleted (archival). Used for audit trail, rollback, and operational safety. Null if not soft-deleted.

ITodoListSystemConfig.IRequest.description:

This type is used as the request body for advanced search, filtering, sorting, and pagination of system configuration entries held in todo_list_system_configs. It supports partial match on key, value search, creation and update date/time filtering, soft deletion filter, and sort or pagination controls for both operational and audit purposes.

All fields are optional to support flexible queries. Designed for privileged admin usage in system administration interfaces.

ITodoListSystemConfig.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for creating a new system-wide configuration entry in the Todo List application.

This DTO is used by privileged administrators to define a global key-value pair that controls overarching system settings, feature toggles, or operational options. Each configuration key must be unique and identifies a specific deployment-level parameter.

The 'value' holds the configuration data (as a string), while the 'description' provides optional documentation and business context for future audit or operational use. Timestamps and UUIDs are system-managed, not client-provided, and are excluded from this create DTO.

key.description: Unique configuration key identifying the system setting. This key must be globally unique across the todo_list_system_configs table. Example values: 'default_timezone', 'feature_maintenance_mode', 'system_banner_message'.

value.description: Configuration value as a string. Represents either a scalar system setting, feature toggle, or a serialized object for more complex options.

description.description: Optional textual explanation of the intent or operational context for this configuration entry. Can be used for documentation, change tracking, or supporting future audits.

ITodoListSystemConfig.IUpdate.description:
Request body schema for updating an existing todo_list_system_configs record.

Used by administrators to modify the value or description of an existing system-wide configuration. This update DTO enables straightforward changes to system settings, feature gates, or operational flags. Updates are applied atomically, with modification timestamps being managed automatically by the backend.

The update operation can be performed via unique configuration key or UUID, depending on the corresponding API operation. Client may provide any combination of value or description to update. Fields are optional, allowing for partial updates. Timestamps, unique keys, or identifiers are not modifiable through this update DTO.

value.description: Updated string value for the configuration entry. May contain scalar configuration data, booleans represented as string, or serialized structures for complex settings. Optional—only include if the value should be changed.

description.description: Updated or new documentation for the configuration entry. Optional; include only if explanation or operational notes are being changed.

ITodoListUser.ISummary.description:

ITodoListUserSession.IRequest.description:

referrer.description:

ITodoListUserSession.description:

ITodoListAdmin.ISummary.description:

email.description:
Unique email address of the admin for login and notification.

Must be unique across all administrator accounts. Used for authentication and official notifications related to privileged actions. Must not overlap normal users.

locked.description:
Admin account lock status.

Indicates if the administrator is currently suspended from system access. True if the account is locked for any reason (disciplinary, compliance, etc.), false if active.

role.description:
Administrative role or privilege class (e.g., superadmin, moderator).

Specifies the admin's permission tier and authorizes their scope of actions within the system. Determines access boundaries within admin workflows. Must match recognized roles per business policy.

created_at.description:
Account creation timestamp.

Datetime when the admin account was established in the system. Used for lifecycle tracking and audit history.

updated_at.description:
Time of last admin profile or credential update.

Tracks when any profile data or password was last changed. Supports record history and security audits.

oneOf.description:
Soft deletion timestamp for the admin account.

If the admin account has been soft deleted, this field contains the datetime of deletion. Otherwise, it is null. Used for internal record management and compliance.

deleted_at.description: Soft deletion timestamp for the admin account or null if active.

ITodoListAdmin.description:
Represents administrators with privileged access to system oversight, user management, and moderation.

Admins can view and manage users and any todo in the system, and can impose status/actions such as account locking or deletion for compliance or support. Authentication credentials, unique email, role flags, lifecycle timestamps, and soft deletion status are included. Only privileged personnel are represented; regular users are never present in this table.

The schema strictly follows the todo_list_admins Prisma model. Sensitive authentication data (such as password hashes) is excluded from the API response for security reasons. Used in admin detail queries, audits, and privilege management endpoints.

email.description:
Globally unique email address for the administrator account.

Must not conflict with other admin records. This property can be updated for login or notification changes, but must always remain unique in the system.

password.description:
New plain password for admin authentication.

Provided only when a password change is intended. The backend will hash and store the new value appropriately. Never provide hashed passwords directly in the API request. Passwords must comply with strength requirements set in system policy.

locked.description:
Admin account lock status.

Set to true to suspend admin access or false to re-enable. Used to impose disciplinary restrictions or restore access as needed.

role.description:
Administrative role or access privilege.

Update to change the admin's access tier. Must be an allowed role as defined in system configuration or policy.

oneOf.description: Clear to null to reactivate a previously soft-deleted admin account.

deleted_at.description: If set to null, reactivates a soft-deleted administrator account. Cannot directly set a non-null deletion value from the API.

ITodoListAdmin.IUpdate.description:
Fields for updating an administrator account in the todo_list_admins table.

Allows modification of email (must remain unique and valid), plain password (backend hashes and updates accordingly), lock status (account suspension), administrative role (change of privilege), and recovery from soft deletion (by setting deleted_at to null only).

This DTO strictly follows business policy, enforcing uniqueness constraints and allowed value sets. Passwords are never accepted as pre-hashed strings in the request DTO, only as new plain text values for immediate hashing. Other lifecycle and immutable fields (id, created_at, etc.) cannot be updated via this DTO. Used in PUT /todoList/admin/admins/{adminId} operations for privilege management or account recovery.

ITodoListAdminSession.description:
Administrator session record for auditing privileged login and activity on the todo system.

Represents a single login session for an admin account. Captures metadata such as origin IP address, connection URL, client referrer, session start and end timestamps, and is directly linked to the parent todo_list_admins entity for full traceability and compliance auditing. Used for security monitoring, intrusion detection, investigations, and regulatory reporting.

Returned by session detail and session list API endpoints; never contains authentication secrets or credentials.

id.description: Unique identifier of the session record. The primary key for todo_list_admin_sessions.

admin.description: The administrator account to which this session belongs. Reference to the parent admin entity, provides admin context for auditing.

ip.description: IP address from which the admin initiated the session. Used for geo-location or suspicious access pattern detection.

href.description: Service entry URL associated with the session, identifying the exact endpoint or page where the session started.

referrer.description: HTTP referrer or origin of the initial admin request for this session, used for audit trail and risk assessment.

created_at.description: Timestamp noting when the session was established (ISO 8601, UTC).

expired_at.description: The time when this session expired or was closed. Null if the session is still active.

ITodoListAdminSession.IRequest.description:
Search and filter parameters for querying administrator login sessions across the todo list system.

Used as the request body for endpoints that provide paginated and filterable lists of administrator sessions for a given admin account. Allows detailed audit, security review, and activity analysis workflows by privileged actors.

All properties are optional and may be specified in any combination. Typical filters include IP address, access URL substring, referrer substring, creation date range, and inclusion or exclusion of expired sessions. Pagination is supported via page and limit parameters for large result sets.

page.description:
Page number of the results to retrieve for pagination purposes. Pagination starts from 1.

Optional; if not provided, defaults to the first page. Used by clients to traverse large sets of administrator session records.

limit.description:
Maximum number of session records to return per page of results.

Optional; can be set by the client to control page size (e.g., 10, 20, 50). Helps optimize bandwidth and performance for interactive administrative UIs.

ip.description:
Filter sessions by exact match on the origin IP address.

This parameter is optional. If provided, only sessions that were created from this specific IP address are returned. Used for network forensic investigations and security event correlation.

href.description:
Filter sessions based on access URL, matching either in full or by suffix/substring.

Optional. Useful for scoping session history to certain endpoints or workflow entry points in the system (e.g., admin dashboard login, password reset page, sensitive operations).

referrer.description:
Filter returned sessions by the HTTP referrer or page origin.

Optional. Allows privilege actors to restrict session search to those originating from specific sources or inbound navigation paths (e.g., corporate SSO initiations).

created_at_from.description:
Return only sessions created on or after this timestamp (UTC, ISO 8601).

Optional. Useful for filtering sessions in a particular time window for compliance investigations or incident response. Example: '2025-01-01T00:00:00Z'.

created_at_to.description:
Return only sessions created on or before this timestamp (UTC, ISO 8601).

Optional. Used in conjunction with created_at_from for bounded-range queries. Example: '2025-01-31T23:59:59Z'.

expired.description:
Filter flag to limit results to expired sessions only (sessions with a non-null expired_at field).

Optional. Set to true to only include sessions that are no longer active; omit or set false to retrieve all sessions regardless of expiration state. Provides rapid filtering for session lifecycle management.

ITodoListAdminDeletionLog.description:
Detailed audit log entry documenting the deletion of an administrative account for regulatory compliance and internal security review in the todo list system.

Each entry in this log is generated by a privileged actor (such as a superadmin) or by the system itself and records the removal of an admin account from active use. The log serves as an immutable record supporting compliance with legal, operational, and transparency requirements.

Key data in the log includes the deleted admin's identity, the high-privilege actor responsible for the deletion (if not a self-deletion), narrative or code explanation for the event, and an exact deletion timestamp. The record supports historical inquiry, forensics, and audit retention policies. All fields, data types, and validation rules are drawn from the todo_list_admin_deletion_logs Prisma schema and its documentation. This type is never directly modified except by deletion system workflows and is always read-only in the public API.

id.description:
Primary key universally identifying this deletion log entry.

A unique UUID assigned to each deletion event for traceability and compliance auditing. Corresponds to the 'id' field in the Prisma model.

admin_id.description:
UUID of the administrator account that was deleted in this event.

Maps directly to todo_list_admins.id and supports linking the deletion to the user lifecycle for full audit trail reconstruction. Always present in the log.

deleted_by_admin_id.description:
Optional UUID of the higher-privilege admin who performed the deletion.

If present, indicates a privileged actor removed another admin; for self-deletions this field is null. Maintains a clear distinction between voluntary and externally-enforced account removals.

reason.description:
Narrative, event code, or justification for why the admin account was deleted.

Always present. Allows forensic and compliance teams to evaluate deletion causes and spot possible process or security issues based on descriptive logging.

deleted_at.description:
Precise UTC timestamp when the deletion event fully took effect (ISO 8601 format required).

Drawn from the database 'deleted_at' field. Used for compliance audits, time-based queries, and enforcing retention policies across all administrative account lifecycle events.

ITodoListAdminDeletionLog.IRequest.description:
Search and filter parameters for querying admin account deletion logs for administrative audit, compliance reporting, or internal review workflows.

Supports filtering by admin identity, deletion initiator, time window, and reason. Also supports pagination and sorting for scalable and performant audit workflows as required by log review use cases.

This DTO aligns with compliance-oriented search interfaces for high-volume deletion log lists.

query.description: Free-text search against reasons or target admin information.

reason.description: Specific narrative or event code to filter logs by deletion reason.

deleted_by_admin_id.description: UUID of administrative actor who deleted the account. Filter for specific deleter.

time_from.description: Inclusive lower bound for deletion timestamp; filters logs occurring after this date-time (ISO 8601).

time_to.description: Inclusive upper bound for deletion timestamp; filters logs occurring before or at this date-time (ISO 8601).

page.description: Page number for paginated results (starts from 1).

limit.description: Number of log records to return per page (max 100).

id.description: Primary key for the audit log entry. Globally unique identifier assigned at insertion, ensuring each record is immutable and traceable.

oneOf.description: References the user who performed the action, if a user initiated this event. Nullable; use actor_admin_id for admin actions. {@link todo_list_users.id}.
Null if action was not performed by a user.

actor_user_id.description: References the user who performed the action, if a user initiated this event. Nullable; use actor_admin_id for admin actions. {@link todo_list_users.id}.

oneOf.description: References the admin who performed the action, if admin initiated. Nullable; use actor_user_id for user-initiated events. {@link todo_list_admins.id}.
Null if action was not performed by an admin.

actor_admin_id.description: References the admin who performed the action, if admin initiated. Nullable; use actor_user_id for user-initiated events. {@link todo_list_admins.id}.

oneOf.description: References the user session tied to the action, if event is linked to a user session. Nullable. {@link todo_list_user_sessions.id}.
Null if not linked to a user session.

actor_user_session_id.description: References the user session tied to the action, if event is linked to a user session. Nullable. {@link todo_list_user_sessions.id}.

oneOf.description: References the admin session if the action was performed during an admin session. Nullable. {@link todo_list_admin_sessions.id}.
Null if not linked to an admin session.

actor_admin_session_id.description: References the admin session if the action was performed during an admin session. Nullable. {@link todo_list_admin_sessions.id}.

oneOf.description: References a specific todo if the action/event affects a todo. Nullable for global/auth events not linked to a todo. {@link todo_list_todos.id}.
Null if action/event does not affect a todo item.

affected_todo_id.description: References a specific todo if the action/event affects a todo. Nullable for global/auth events not linked to a todo. {@link todo_list_todos.id}.

event_action.description: Describes the action taken or event type (e.g., 'todo_create', 'todo_edit', 'user_login', 'admin_lock_user', 'permission_denied'). Application-defined event type for robust filtering and analytics.

event_status.description: Result status of the event ('success', 'failure', 'denied', etc). Enables filtering audit logs by outcome and error/failure reporting in compliance reviews.

oneOf.description: Free-form context data (JSON or string) capturing additional details—affected columns, before/after state, request metadata, error codes. Used for deep auditing, investigation, or legal review. Can be null if event has no extra context.
Null if event has no extra context.

event_context.description: Free-form context data (JSON or string) capturing additional details—affected columns, before/after state, request metadata, error codes. Used for deep auditing, investigation, or legal review. Can be null if event has no extra context.

oneOf.description: IP address of the actor/session generating the event, if available. Nullable.
Null if IP address unavailable.

ip_address.description: IP address of the actor/session generating the event, if available. Nullable.

oneOf.description: User agent string (browser/app version) from HTTP request, if captured. Nullable. Supports threat analysis and anomaly detection.
Null if user agent unavailable.

user_agent.description: User agent string (browser/app version) from HTTP request, if captured. Nullable. Supports threat analysis and anomaly detection.

created_at.description: Timestamp (UTC) when the audit event was logged. Immutable and required for all records. Used for temporal queries, trending, and compliance timelines.

ITodoListAuditLog.description:
Audit log of security-relevant, admin, and business actions across the todo system.

This type represents a single, immutable record in the audit log—capturing every important operation or event that may impact system security, user privacy, admin oversight, or compliance. Each record references the acting identity (user or admin), the affected todo (if applicable), session, and includes detailed metadata for compliance, investigations, and operational monitoring.

Entries in this type are append-only—never deleted or updated—to ensure strict traceability. The schema includes rich context and outcome metadata for security investigation and business reporting purposes.

event_action.description: Filter actions by event type—application-defined (e.g., 'todo_create', 'user_login', 'permission_denied'). Partial matches and wildcards may be supported.

actor_user_id.description: User ID acting as event initiator. Filter audit logs performed by a specific user. Use only one of user or admin actor at a time.

actor_admin_id.description: Admin ID acting as event initiator. Filter on actions performed by a specific administrator.

affected_todo_id.description: Filter logs by affected todo item. Only logs referencing this todo will be included.

since.description: Lower bound (inclusive, ISO 8601 UTC) for searching audit logs by event creation time.

until.description: Upper bound (inclusive, ISO 8601 UTC) for searching audit logs by event creation time.

page.description: Page number for paginated results. Starts at 1.

page_size.description: Number of audit logs per page. Limited to protect against excessive result volume.

sort_by.description: Field to sort audit logs by. Currently only 'created_at' is supported.

oneOf.description: Sort order for the results: ascending or descending by the sort field. Default is 'desc' for latest event first.
Sort order for the results: ascending or descending by the sort field. Default is 'desc' for latest event first.

sort_direction.description: Sort order for the results: ascending or descending by the sort field. Default is 'desc' for latest event first.

ITodoListAuditLog.IRequest.description:
Audit log search and filter request parameters supporting event action, status, actor roles, target entity, time range, sorting, and pagination.

This type provides all filters and options supported by the admin audit log search interface, covering event actions, outcomes, actor filtering (user or admin), target todo, time ranges, and pagination/sorting. Only privileged admin actors are authorized to use this request type. No destructive or write actions are possible—strictly safe for query and investigation.

ITodoListTodo.description:
Represents an individual todo item for a single end-user as modeled by the todo_list_todos Prisma table.

Each todo item corresponds to an actionable task with immutable ownership, enforced by a foreign key to the user. Contains core task data—title, description, status—as well as system-managed timestamps for creation, update, and (optionally) completion. Optional fields (description, due_date, completed_at) are supported as nullable, enabling a flexible workflow.

Use this type for reading full details of a user's todo item, supporting business rules defined in the schema. All validation for state transitions, field formats, and owner enforcement is handled server-side. Ownership is always private to the authenticated user and never modifiable via the API. No collaborative or group features exist for todo items. Hard deletion is expected per requirements.

id.description: Primary Key. Uniquely identifies each todo item.

title.description: Todo title. Required and validated for non-whitespace content during creation and update. Must be between 1 and 100 characters.

description.description: Optional description for the todo item. Can be set to a string with a maximum of 1000 characters or null. Absence or null means the item has no description.

oneOf.description: Status of the todo item. One of: 'pending', 'completed', or 'archived'. Status changes enforce business lifecycle transitions and auditability.
Status of the todo item. One of: 'pending', 'completed', or 'archived'. Status changes enforce business lifecycle transitions and auditability.

due_date.description: Optional due date in ISO 8601 format. Null if unset. Must not be in the past for creation/update per business rules.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the todo item was created (UTC, system-managed). Immutable once set.

updated_at.description: Timestamp for the last time the todo item was updated (UTC, system-managed). Changes whenever any updatable field is modified.

completed_at.description: Timestamp when the item was marked as completed. Null unless the status is 'completed'.

todo_list_user_id.description: Foreign key referencing the owning user in todo_list_users. Immutable and never updatable via API requests. Guarantees private ownership and scoping.

title.description: Todo title. Required for creation and update. Must be between 1 and 100 characters in length and validated for non-whitespace content. Business logic enforces that the title cannot consist only of whitespace and must be unique within the user's todos.

oneOf.description: Optional todo description, allowing up to 1000 characters. Can be omitted or set to null during creation or update.

description.description: Optional todo description. Maximum 1000 characters. This property can be omitted or set to null.

oneOf.description: Initial status of the todo item. Permitted values are 'pending', 'completed', or 'archived'. Business rules enforce proper lifecycle transitions and default to 'pending' if not provided explicitly.

oneOf.description: Optional due date in ISO 8601 format (UTC). If provided, must not be in the past at creation.

due_date.description: Optional due date for the todo item as an ISO 8601 datetime string (UTC). May be omitted or set to null. If specified, the value must not be earlier than the current date/time at the time of creation.

ITodoListTodo.ICreate.description: DTO for creating a new individual todo item for an authenticated user. Used as the request body for creating todos. Includes required title and status, and optional description and due date. The item's ownership is enforced by context and is not included as a property. All business and validation rules are documented in the schema and enforced server-side.

title.description: New title for the todo. Must be 1–100 characters and not all whitespace when present. If omitted, the title will not be updated.

oneOf.description: Update for the description, allowing up to 1000 characters. May be set to null to remove the description.

description.description: Update for the todo's description. Up to 1000 characters, or null to clear. Field is optional.

oneOf.description: Update to the todo's status. Permitted transitions are enforced by business logic; legal values are 'pending', 'completed', and 'archived'. Optional: omit if not updating status.

due_date.description: Update to the due date for this todo. ISO 8601 date. May be cleared with null. Field is optional.

ITodoListTodo.IUpdate.description: DTO for updating an existing todo item belonging to the authenticated user. Used as the request body for updating. All fields are optional, and system will only update those provided. Enforces business validation for title, description, status, and due date. Ownership and all security rules are enforced by context.

ITodoListTodo.ISummary.description:
Summary DTO representing an individual todo item for usage in list views, search results, and embeddings.

Provides core fields of a todo, including its unique identifier, title, status, and critical timeline fields, deliberately omitting large text fields and composition arrays for list performance. Belongs-to references are transformed as contextual summary information (such as user), but strong composition or unbounded aggregations are excluded.

Intended for high-frequency atomic read operations and optimized to enable UI clients to display single or batched todo items without requiring additional API calls for essential information. Designed to reflect all data constraints and business rules present in the underlying Prisma model, notably those tied to immutable ownership, mandatory status, and timestamp lifecycle tracking.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the todo item.

Primary key for "todo_list_todos" table. Universally unique and immutable once assigned. Used to reference todo objects programmatically.

title.description: Todo title column. Required for creation and update operations. Between 1 and 100 characters (inclusive); validated for non-whitespace content. Describes the main actionable content of the todo item visible to the user.

oneOf.description:
Status/state of the todo item.

Allowed values: "pending", "completed", or "archived". Enforces the business lifecycle transitions of a todo. Determines available actions in UI and triggers lifecycle hooks in backend. Value updated on creation, completion, or archiving per specification.

Status/state of the todo item.

Allowed values: "pending", "completed", or "archived". Enforces the business lifecycle transitions of a todo. Determines available actions in UI and triggers lifecycle hooks in backend. Value updated on creation, completion, or archiving per specification.

due_date.description: Optional due date in ISO 8601 format, stored as UTC. If omitted or not set, will be null. Enforced on creation/update to be in the future or null.

completed_at.description: Timestamp when the todo was marked as completed. Nullable; null if the todo is not completed. Only set when status transitions to 'completed'. Used for audit and UI display.

created_at.description: Timestamp for when the todo item was created, stored as UTC. Immutable after initial insert. Used for data lifecycle, ordering, audit, and analytics.

updated_at.description: Timestamp for the last modification of the todo item. Changes on every update action (title, description, status, due_date change). Maintains user and system accountability.

ITodoListTodo.IRequest.description:
Request schema for searching, filtering, and paginating the current user's todo items.

Supports keyword search in title/description, status filtering, due/created date ranges, and full pagination and sort options. All queries are scoped to the authenticated user. Used as the request body for PATCH /todoList/user/todos.

ITodoListSystemConfig.ISummary.description:
Summary information for a system-wide configuration entry in the Todo List application.

This schema provides the minimal required and highly relevant fields for listing, monitoring, and reviewing global configuration settings in administrative interfaces. It now includes the configuration key and value as well as associated audit and operational fields—such as creation and update timestamps, and optional deletion status—for robust traceability and operational oversight.

Used in admin dashboards and configuration list views where quick access to both current values and operational metadata is necessary. The presence of timestamps enables administrators to track changes and soft deletion for safe config management and historical forensics.

key.description:
Unique configuration key identifying the system setting. Example values include 'default_timezone' and 'feature_maintenance_mode'. Must be unique for each configuration in the table.

Represents the business-level name of this option and is required for all system configuration entries.

value.description:
Configuration value as a string, representing the effective setting for this key. May be a scalar value or a serialized option depending on business requirements.

Directly reflects the current operational value set in the backend system. Only basic data types or safe-serialized JSON objects are supported.

description.description: Optional detailed description of this configuration entry. Null if not provided; included to aid understanding in administrative lists. This field is a free-form business/technical annotation.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the configuration entry was created, in ISO 8601 format.

Useful for audit trails, real-time monitoring, and investigation of system state at any moment in time. Mandatory and non-nullable, directly mirrors the Prisma model's created_at.

updated_at.description:
Timestamp when this configuration entry was last updated, in ISO 8601 format.

Tracked for every modification to allow administrators to see recent changes and ensure accountability. Required and always present due to schema constraints.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp indicating soft deletion of the configuration entry. If null, the configuration is active; if set, the config has been archived or removed from use but retained for operational safety and rollback. Nullable and optional per the Prisma schema for safe rotation and recovery.

id.description:
Primary key for the deletion log entry.

Unique identifier that distinguishes this user deletion log from all others. Used for referencing and traceability in audit and compliance workflows.
Sources from the todo_list_user_deletion_logs Prisma model primary field.

user_id.description:
ID of the user who was deleted. Links to the todo_list_users table.

Essential for audit, compliance, and tracing account deletion events for a specific user.

deleted_by_admin_id.description:
ID of the administrator who performed the account deletion.

If null, indicates the user deleted their own account (self-deletion scenario). Used for differentiating between admin and self-initiated deletions. Nullable in Prisma schema.

reason.description:
Reason for the account deletion (GDPR, user request, admin suspension, etc).

Captures the business, regulatory, or compliance justification for deleting the user. Populated by the workflow that triggers the deletion.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp when the account deletion event occurred.

Stored in ISO 8601 format for compliance with audit log standards. Used as a temporal anchor for lifecycle event analysis.

ITodoListUserDeletionLog.ISummary.description:
Summary type for user deletion logs in the todo-list system.

Contains audit information about when, why, and by whom a user deletion event was performed. Used in list views and reporting endpoints where a lightweight summary of deletion activity is sufficient. Does not include parent user or admin object—only IDs for tracing.

ITodoListAdminDeletionLog.ISummary.description:
Summary view for an administrative deletion log entry.

Provides a condensed view of administrative deletion events recorded for audit, forensic, and compliance use cases. Each summary describes the deleted admin, the actor (if not self-deletion), the stated reason, and when the deletion was performed. Used for list endpoints, dashboards, and administrative review pages.

Summaries support filtering, compliance auditing, and quick user lifecycle reviews. No sensitive or redundant information is included beyond what is necessary for summary display and business analytics.

id.description: Globally unique identifier for this deletion log entry. Used to identify and reference specific events.

admin_id.description: Unique identifier of the admin whose account was deleted. References todo_list_admins.id.

deleted_by_admin_id.description: ID of the higher privilege admin who performed this deletion, if any. Null if self-deletion.

reason.description: Narrative or code for the account deletion cause. Explains why this admin account was removed, for compliance or audit review.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp (UTC) when the admin account was deleted. Used for sorting, auditing, and timeline analytics.

ITodoListAuditLog.ISummary.description:
Summary view for an audit log entry of system, security, or business actions.

A compact, human-readable representation of key event details for display in audit lists, searches, and compliance interfaces. Used to quickly scan logged operations without full context payloads.

Includes actor/user/admin, session, affected todo (if any), action type and status, timestamps, and context data hint. Does not contain sensitive payloads beyond what is required for monitoring and legal/compliance review summaries.

id.description: Globally unique identifier for the audit log entry.

actor_user_id.description: References the user who performed the action if user-initiated. Null for admin/system events.

actor_admin_id.description: References the admin who performed the action if admin-initiated. Null for user/system events.

actor_user_session_id.description: Authentication session (user) during which the event occurred. Null if not applicable.

actor_admin_session_id.description: Authentication session (admin) during which the event occurred. Null if not applicable.

affected_todo_id.description: Affected todo entity if event is related to a specific item. Null otherwise.

event_action.description: Action or event type label (e.g., 'todo_create', 'user_login', 'permission_denied'). Application-defined.

event_context.description: Extra event context (could be a JSON string or explanation), providing further audit or investigation details. Null if none.

ip_address.description: IP address from which the event originated, if available. Null otherwise.

user_agent.description: Browser/app user agent string from the HTTP request, if recorded. Null otherwise.

created_at.description: Timestamp (UTC) when this audit log entry was created.
